- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–5 days; apply downward drag of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint of sentiment transition.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast deviates >2% from 14-day moving average, adjust toward it.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in horizon (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap early forecast peaks at 1.5–2% below true 30d mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days for smoothing.
